To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the three systems of additive tree biomass models were developed for natural Mongolian oak and the carbon concentration varied depending on the tree components and tree growing regions in Northeastern China.

the three systems of additive model systems were developed and the regional respective component biomass carbon concentration was the best approach to estimate the carbon stock of natural Mongolian oak in northeastern China.
the aggregated model systems with or without parameter restrictions are suitable for estimating tree biomass and carbon storage in natural oak forest in Northeast China.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an aggregated model system that can be used to predict the biomass of Mongolian oak and the associated carbon stock in Northeastern China.
the development of a new method for carbon stock estimation of tree components in natural forests.
the development of a new method for estimating carbon storage in natural forests of Northeast China and provides a new approach for carbon estimation in other regions of the world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AMS3 model system with D, H and CL as predictor combinations was the best among the three systems and the regional carbon concentration was a better approach than using the mean carbon concentration for carbon stock quantification.
AMS0 is the most robust system and the AMS1 system is the second most robust system for estimating tree carbon stock of Mongolian oak.
all of the AMS models are good choices for estimating tree biomass in the study region and the AMS0 is the best choice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AMS0 model with D, D, and H as the predictor variables is the most appropriate model for estimating the carbon stock of the natural Mongolian oak forests in Northeastern China.
, the AMS1 model is recommended for the estimation of tree biomass and carbon stock for Mongolian oak in the natural forests.
the additive model system with one parameter restriction was the best model for estimating biomass and carbon stocks of natural Mongolian oak.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AMS0 system with three predictor combinations (D D H, CL) is the most suitable for estimating carbon stocks of Mongolian oaks in the natural forests.
the AMS0 model system with the D, H, CL format is the most robust and reliable model for estimating biomass and carbon stock in Mongolian oak forests in Northeastern China.
the additive biomass model systems developed herein can be applied to estimate the total biomass and carbon stock of Mongolian oak.
